rows.quote: We used the latest release data on VTE from the FinnGen study R12 in this analysis, which comprised 26,333 cases 474,015 controls.
rows.coder_note: The sentence names the release, FinnGen study R12 (26,333 cases and 474,015 controls); the FinnGen data are used as their own replication dataset, and the authors' later meta-analysis with the UK Biobank GWAS is not one of the FinnGen meta-analysis rows.

rows.quote: GWAS data for VTE were assessed from UK biobank database (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/studies/GCST90038607) [14].
rows.coder_note: Rule B: the sentence names the dataset by the GWAS Catalog accession GCST90038607 (reference 14, Dönertaş 2021), which no dictionary row lists.

Reference 12 (Sun 2023) has four dictionary rows; the attributes in the sentence (54,306 participants, 1,463 proteins, Olink) match the sample size of none of them, and no ancestry or subcohort is given.

rows.quote: Comparatively, the deCODE Health study employed SomaScan platform to measure 4,907 proteomic aptamers in 35,559 Icelandic individuals, identifying instrumentally valid cis-SNPs for 1,423 plasma proteins [13].
rows.reference_quote: Ferkingstad E Sulem P Atlason BA Sveinbjornsson G Magnusson MI Styrmisdottir EL Large-scale integration of the plasma proteome with genetics and disease Nat Genet 2021 53 1712 1721 10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w 34857953
rows.coder_note: The deCODE data (SomaScan, 4,907 aptamers, 35,559 Icelanders) are attributed to reference 13, whose DOI 10.1038/s41588-021-00978-w and PMID 34857953 are those of the Ferkingstad 2021 row alone.
